held_records.reason: Primary178 and secondary26 Q65 allow Student Affairs as an institutional compound and Students’ Affairs as a possessive phrase. The office’s formal name is not supplied, so punctuation cannot decide a unique answer.
Primary178 prints Many candidates but secondary26 prints Many a candidate. Even the latter can take fails or is failing with different valid aspects; there is no time cue excluding the progressive.
Primary178 and secondary26 Q67 offer implied and suggested for expressing something indirectly. Both fit the denial of an explicit description; no wording resolves the overlapping meanings.
Primary179 and secondary26 Q72 offer may as well and might as well. Both established constructions fit the suggestion to finish a journey already mostly completed.
Primary179 and secondary26 Q73 offer blurred and defective sight. Both explain wearing corrective glasses, and the sentence supplies no diagnosis distinguishing them.
Primary179 and secondary26 Q76 offer alternate and alternative. Alternate is established, especially in American English, for a substitute arrangement; no British-only usage rule is specified.
Primary180 and secondary26 Q77 allow stuck a needle in and stuck a needle into. Both prepositions can express insertion in this construction, so the options overlap.

Primary180 and secondary27 Q81 allow both examinations started before he arrived and examinations had started before he arrived. Before already marks the sequence, so the simple past is also grammatical.
